items.rationale: Every model call is separate and the model keeps no state; the program re-sends the history (the messages list) on each call. Options b, c and d each assume the model or provider holds memory between calls (M7).

Call 1 sends 800 + 200 = 1,000 tokens. Call 2 re-sends all of that plus the 30-token request and 600-token result: 1,630. Total 1,000 + 1,630 = 2,630. An answer of 1,830 (adding only the new text once) shows the history is not re-sent each call (M7).

Memory between sessions is text the program saves outside the window and loads in later. A large window (a) cannot outlast the session (M8); a prompt instruction (c) gives the model nothing to remember; a model does not keep chats after a session (d, M7).

items.answer: It is cheaper and more focused: every token in the context is paid for on every call, and irrelevant text crowds the window and distracts the model, so only the few relevant chunks should go in.

items.rationale: Full credit for any one valid reason: cost (tokens re-sent on every call), the window limit, or noise from irrelevant text. Saying a larger window makes pasting fine shows M8.
The messages list and tool results live in the context, which ends with the session. The search index, calendar system and notes file are stored outside it and persist.
